Name any color on your screen
DaltonPick waits as a small tab on the edge of your screen. Pull it out and a round lens appears. Put the crosshair on any color and the lens tells you its name, like “Olive green” or “Dusty rose”.
Screen images stay on your phone. They are never saved or sent anywhere.
To see colors in other apps, DaltonPick uses an accessibility service.
Android will warn that the service can see your screen. DaltonPick only looks when you pull the lens, and never saves or sends what it sees.
In Accessibility settings, open DaltonPick and turn it on.
Allow notifications to get a quiet notification with Hide and Settings buttons. You can also add a Quick Settings tile.
Pull the tab on the edge of the screen toward the middle, then move the lens over these colors. Tap the tab to put the lens away.
The lens is off, so you can’t try it yet. You can turn it on later from the home screen.
You can change the lens size, zoom and edge in Settings.
